ruling.recommended_action: Refund $2.74 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) for the unexempted off-route segment; record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file. No account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI, so the fare model is per-km and detour mileage flows into the meter (RD-0/preamble; F6). The GPS record establishes one off-route segment 09:47–09:53, 3.83 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.89 km, +1.94 km, straying up to 777 m [F3]; trip-wide the actual 13.1 km exceeds the 10.7 km optimal route by 2.4 km [F1]. Under RD-1 that unexplained deviation breaches the driver's shortest-and-most-direct obligation.

No exemption applies. There is no traffic incident near the route in the trip window [F12], and the only speed-band records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Ayer Rajah Expressway and Kent Ridge Road [F10][F11], which is neither an RD-4(a) incident nor a band 1–2 condition, so RD-4 does not excuse the segment; fair weather with 0.0 mm rain removes any other reasonable cause [F13].

No consent exempts it. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped and contains a single rider message at 09:35 about the kerb outside Mandarin Gallery and a red jacket [F7][F8] — no route instruction of any kind, and it predates but does not address the segment. The driver's post-trip statement "I followed my GPS; it rerouted me. Nothing wrong with the fare." [F9] is a claim appearing only in his own statement, which is not consent under RD-5 (G11). The rider sent no message agreeing to a route before the segment began, so the finding under RD-5 is that the segment counts. No rider-requested stop is recorded in the segment, so RD-3 grants nothing [F3][F7].

Amount: RD-2 refunds Σ unexempted extra_km × this trip's per-km rate, and the rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km: $18.50 ÷ 13.12 km = $1.4101/km [F6]. Applied to the segment's 1.94 km extra [F3]: 1.94 km × $1.4101/km = $2.7364 → $2.74. The larger $3.44 "excess distance billed" line (2.44 km × $1.4101) [F4] includes ~0.50 km not attributed to any segment [F1], which RD-2 expressly leaves unrefunded, so recovery is capped at $2.74.

RD-6 does not apply: the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (2 disputes, 1 upheld, none route) [F15], so this case does not make him "repeated" on the route dimension, and profile facts cannot decide the case anyway [F14][F15]. No flag_account.

Safety screen: I read the rider's message [F7], the driver's statement [F9] and the complaint — a locator ("I'll find you at the kerb outside Mandarin Gallery"), a factual fare denial and a refund request. No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so this is not a SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation.

Evidence: the record settles every element the ruling needs — measured segment [F3], fare and rate [F4][F6], complete timestamped chat [F8], incident screen [F12], profile [F15].

segment_findings.reason: The 09:47–09:53 segment (+1.94 km, up to 777 m off route) is not exempted. RD-5 requires a RIDER message sent before the segment agreeing to the route: the only rider message is the 09:35 kerb meeting note [F7], in a complete timestamped record [F8], which says nothing about any route, and the driver's post-trip 'my GPS rerouted me' claim [F9] is not consent (G11). No rider-requested named stop under RD-3 appears in the segment. No traffic incident or band 1–2 corroboration exists, so RD-4 does not excuse it (F12, F10, F11). The segment is therefore an unexempted detour under RD-1 and refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Accepted only in part: the segment exists and is 1.94 km extra [F3][F1], but RD-1's consequence runs through RD-2, which caps recovery at the segment's extra_km rather than the trip-wide +2.4 km — so the claim cannot be read as endorsing the full excess distance.

Rejected as to amount: 'the unexempted 1.94 km of detour flowed into the meter' is right in principle but the $3.44 line is computed on 2.44 km [F4], and RD-2 refunds only the 1.94 km attributed to the segment [F3]; the residual ~0.50 km of unmatched mileage is expressly not refunded.
Accepted as a concession: no RD-4 exemption exists on this record [F12][F10][F11], so the driver cannot rely on traffic as a reasonable cause for the segment.
Accepted as a concession: the driver's own brief confirms there is no pre-segment rider consent [F7][F8][F9], so RD-5 does not exempt the segment.
Accepted: RD-6's repeated-route condition is not met because route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F15], so no flag_account arises and profile facts decide nothing [F14].
